business_problem: Hello Group was handling more than 500,000 service complaints a day across complex mobility transactions, but liability assignment was not accurate enough and customer-service operations were expensive. The company also wanted stronger pre-sales guidance for rental transactions so a large-model agent could improve GMV rather than only automate reactive support.
solution_summary: Hello Group built a transaction robot on Alibaba Cloud Bailian using a portfolio of Qwen-Plus, Qwen-Turbo, and Qwen2-7B-Instruct models. The robot spans pre-sales, in-sales, and after-sales steps of the mobility transaction chain, combining user-intent recognition, multi-turn conversation, intelligent Q&A, and liability handling into one business-facing service. To make the system practical inside production workflows, the team introduced RAG, chain-of-thought, and tool-calling patterns so the agent can retrieve policy or scenario context, reason across transaction states, and take guided actions in support and sales flows. Instead of treating the LLM as a sidecar chatbot, Hello embedded the agent directly into the transaction process, using different Qwen models for responsiveness and capability tradeoffs. That design turned the robot into both a service-efficiency layer and a revenue-oriented guide for rental scenarios.

solution_components.name: Bailian
solution_components.role: Hosts and orchestrates the model portfolio and agent-building workflow for the transaction robot.

solution_components.name: Qwen-Plus
solution_components.role: Handles higher-complexity reasoning tasks inside the transaction robot.

solution_components.name: Qwen-Turbo
solution_components.role: Supports lower-latency conversation and response steps across the transaction chain.

solution_components.name: Qwen2-7B-Instruct
solution_components.role: Provides additional model capacity for specialized transaction-robot tasks.

data_flow: User requests from pre-sales, order-processing, and after-sales scenarios are routed into the Bailian agent layer, where the appropriate Qwen model is selected. RAG and tool-calling components retrieve policy or order context, the agent reasons over the transaction state, and the output is returned as guidance, liability decisions, or customer-service responses embedded in the business workflow.
business_outcome: Hello Group turned the transaction robot into a full-chain service and growth lever. The Alibaba Cloud implementation reduced customer- service operating cost by more than 30%, improved rental-car GMV by 5% in guided sales scenarios, and lifted liability-decision accuracy to 87%+, which reduced complaints while improving the user experience across complex mobility transactions.
architecture_clues: Multiple Qwen models are used together so different transaction tasks can balance cost, latency, and reasoning depth.
RAG, chain-of-thought, and tool-calling are part of the production agent design rather than offline experimentation.
The agent is embedded directly into pre-sales, in-sales, and after-sales steps instead of being limited to a standalone chatbot.
The system targets both service-cost reduction and GMV growth in the same architecture.
